The source lock named obsolete MIND and TestForge commits and did not declare an enforceable tree algorithm; current published commits and recomputed canonical/imported digests are now verifier-enforced.
The combined package did not directly exercise TestForge's metered-capacity authority boundary; the 14-case regression suite is now part of the 43-test repository gate.
The combined builder still expected MIND's superseded README link; it now translates the current user-guide link and a regression binds that link to a real source file.

The downloadable documentation linked to source-lock evidence that the archive omitted; the builder now packages the public package map and source lock, and release link verification enforces the resulting customer path.

The new cross-platform workflow invoked MIND's isolated wheel builder without installing its declared deterministic build requirements; the workflow now installs the same bounded prerequisites as MIND's passing upstream gate, and a repository regression preserves the step.

The release documentation could imply that TestForge itself grants paid authority; the current wording makes the assessor advisory and the trusted external dispatcher responsible for resolving and consuming any later human decision.
Repository workflows used deprecated action majors and duplicate line-ending runs; current majors and one pull-request plus one main-merge execution path are now documented and configured.
